email.subject: Amherst metering: delivery + ultrasonic OEM scope
email.initial:
Hi Timothy,

I’m assessing a potential Metercor–Badger Meter bundle for Amherst’s RFP-26-09. Badger’s ultrasonic E-Series range and Metercor’s Canadian metering services look complementary, subject to the exact approved configuration.

The Town expects to install most meters. The useful joint scope may be supply, data integration, training and support; lead qualifications and product/territory authorization need checking.

Do you cover Canadian municipal metering, or could you point me to the right channel or bid owner? If there is a fit, I’d ask both sides before arranging an introduction with Scott McIntyre. Neither side has committed.

If this is outside your remit, a referral would help. If you would prefer no further emails, please let me know.
followups:
Hi Timothy,

Following up on Amherst RFP-26-09 water metering. The first question is whether Metercor would add a distinct, necessary work package. For your side, I had in mind: ultrasonic meter OEM and approved communications/software configuration.

Is that a useful scope to explore, or should I speak with another owner?

Hi Timothy,

A practical agenda for the proposed Metercor discussion would be: meter size/approval matrix; endpoint compatibility; network coverage; billing export; warranty; phased acceptance. The output could be a one-page responsibility and evidence matrix before either firm spends time on a bid.

Which interface or qualification would you want to resolve first?

Hi Timothy,

For Amherst RFP-26-09 water metering, I would keep the commercial discussion tied to an agreed work package, acceptance criteria and delivery capacity. There is no assumed award, fee split or partner commitment.

Would you be comfortable assessing a possible introduction with Scott McIntyre at Metercor, once the access and scope questions are resolved?

Hi Timothy,

I’ll close this proposed Metercor introduction for now. If a technical discussion would be useful, let me know the right owner and I can coordinate once both sides agree. If this tender is not a fit, a brief “not this one” is enough.

If you prefer no further emails, please let me know.
